#

# only that shell will be killed by the oom monitor instead of the entire                                      
# Ghostty process. Similarly, if a shell program is using too much CPU,                                        
# only that surface will be CPU-throttled.                                                                     
#                                                                                                              
# This will cause startup times to be slower (a hundred milliseconds or so),                                   
# so the default value is "single-instance." In single-instance mode, only                                     
# one instance of Ghostty is running (see gtk-single-instance) so the startup                                  
# time is a one-time cost. Additionally, single instance Ghostty is much                                       
# more likely to have many windows, tabs, etc. so cgroup isolation is a                                        
# big benefit.                                                                                                 
#                                                                                                              
# This feature requires systemd. If systemd is unavailable, cgroup                                             
# initialization will fail. By default, this will not prevent Ghostty                                          
# from working (see linux-cgroup-hard-fail).                                                                   
#                                                                                                              
# Valid values are:                                                                                            
#                                                                                                              
#   * `never` - Never use cgroups.                                                                             
#   * `always` - Always use cgroups.                                                                           
#   * `single-instance` - Enable cgroups only for Ghostty instances launched                                   
#     as single-instance applications (see gtk-single-instance).

#                                                                                                              
# This makes it so that resource management can be done on a per-surface                                       
# granularity. For example, if a shell program is using too much memory,                                       
# only that shell will be killed by the oom monitor instead of the entire                                      
# Ghostty process. Similarly, if a shell program is using too much CPU,                                        
# only that surface will be CPU-throttled.                                                                     
#                                                                                                              
# This will cause startup times to be slower (a hundred milliseconds or so),                                   
# so the default value is "single-instance." In single-instance mode, only                                     
# one instance of Ghostty is running (see gtk-single-instance) so the startup                                  
# time is a one-time cost. Additionally, single instance Ghostty is much                                       
# more likely to have many windows, tabs, etc. so cgroup isolation is a                                        
# big benefit.                                                                                                 
#                                                                                                              
# This feature requires systemd. If systemd is unavailable, cgroup                                             
# initialization will fail. By default, this will not prevent Ghostty                                          
# from working (see linux-cgroup-hard-fail).                                                                   
#                                                                                                              
# Valid values are:                                                                                            
#                                                                                                              
#   * `never` - Never use cgroups.                                                                             
#   * `always` - Always use cgroups.                                                                           
#   * `single-instance` - Enable cgroups only for Ghostty instances launched                                   
#     as single-instance applications (see gtk-single-instance).

# pressure.

Web search results for "ghostty keybind conditional selection SIGINT":

Ghostty's keybinding system allows for conditional behavior, which can be used to manage `Ctrl+C` for both copying selected text and sending a `SIGINT` signal.

To achieve this, you can use the `performable:` prefix in your Ghostty configuration. This prefix ensures that a keybinding's action is only executed if it can be performed. If the action cannot be performed, Ghostty will behave as if no keybind was set for that particular key combination, allowing the default terminal behavior (like sending `SIGINT`) to occur.[1]

For `Ctrl+C`, you would configure it to perform the `copy_to_clipboard` action conditionally. When text is selected, `Ctrl+C` will copy it. If no text is selected, the `copy_to_clipboard` action is not performable, and thus `Ctrl+C` will be passed through to the shell, triggering a `SIGINT`.[1][2]

Add the following line to your Ghostty configuration file (typically located at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ghostty/config` or `$HOME/.config/ghostty/config`):[3]

```
keybind = performable:ctrl+c=copy_to_clipboard
```

This configuration ensures that:
*   If you have text selected, pressing `Ctrl+C` will copy the selection to the clipboard.[1]
*   If no text is selected, pressing `Ctrl+C` will send a `SIGINT` signal to the foreground process in the terminal, effectively interrupting it.[1][2]
